droppedAngles.title: migrations-and-rollout
droppedAngles.why: The diff touches only README.md, src/serialize.js, src/server.js, and test/server.test.js. The `audit` collection, its SCHEMA entry, and the migrations directory (001-init.js, 002-account-currency.js) are all unchanged and pre-date this PR (confirmed via `git diff --stat` against the prior commit and `git log` on src/audit.js and src/store.js). No schema change, no backfill, no deploy-order concern exists in this diff.

droppedAngles.title: silent-drops
droppedAngles.why: This PR adds a purely read-only endpoint — it performs zero new writes to the store. `record()`, the audit schema, and `store.insert`/`pick` are all untouched. There is no new value being written anywhere in this diff for a store or serializer to silently discard; the only new code is a filter+map over data already durably written by pre-existing code paths.

droppedAngles.title: security
droppedAngles.why: No SQL/HTML/URL injection surface (the only user-controlled input, params[0], is used solely as a string key into an in-memory array via getOwnAccount, never interpolated into a path, query, shell command, or template), no secrets touched, no redirects, no CORS changes, and no data sent to any third party. The route regex (`[^/]+`) is a simple bounded character class with no backtracking risk.

droppedAngles.title: data-integrity
droppedAngles.why: No concurrency, caching, or partial-failure surface is introduced: the handler is a single synchronous read (two array scans, a Set build, a filter+map) with no awaited I/O in between, so there is no interleaving or torn-state window. The full-table scan over `audit` on every call is a pre-existing architectural pattern already shared by the unpaginated sibling route `/accounts/:id/transfers`, not something this diff newly introduces.

scoutNotes: Adds a read-only GET /accounts/:id/audit that aggregates audit-log entries targeting the account itself plus each of its transfers, returning only {action, at} (actor deliberately hidden), gated by the existing owner-only getOwnAccount check. The diff touches only README.md, src/serialize.js (new publicAuditEntry), src/server.js (new route), and test/server.test.js (one new integration test) — no changes to audit.js, store.js, accounts.js, or transfers.js, which already defined the audit collection, schema, and record()/entriesFor() helpers this route builds on.
